script: What punishments are Manchester City most likely to face now that they've been found guilty? Manchester City have just been found guilty on 114 out of 115 charges for breaking the Premier League's financial rules, with the charges covering nine years of alleged fraud from 2009 to 2018, the same stretch where City lifted three Premier League titles. But here's why the punishment could be unlike anything we've ever seen in English football. Firstly, David Ornstein of The Athletic reported that so far, no sanctions have been decided, yet all possibilities remain on the table, including stripped titles, although that seems unlikely according to Ornstein's article that just came out with The Athletic. What's a lot more likely is a points deduction. Now, Everton got a six-point deduction and Forest had four points stripped for breaches that were far smaller on scale. City's case has over 100 guilty verdicts spanning nearly a decade, and football finance expert Kieran Maguire has said a deduction of somewhere between 40 and 60 points would be the logical punishment to stay consistent with those earlier decisions, which would almost certainly send any team to the bottom of the table, no matter how well they play. On top of that, the commission could impose a transfer ban or, in the most extreme case, expel them from the league entirely, although I personally can't picture them getting expelled. But there's actually one more thing that could cost City a lot of money. Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester United, and Spurs all filed legal notices back in 2024 to claim compensation for the damage City caused them. For reference, Burnley already won over $47 million from Everton for a far smaller breach. So these legal notices could cost City hundreds of millions of dollars. And at the end of the day, City are expected to appeal, which could push a final resolution back another six to 12 months. But right now, things are looking really bad for them, and it's almost like a few of their key departures this summer saw this coming.
